lines: +# Attribution notes
+Principle: a verifier verdict is the policy's (`policy`, zeros included)
+unless there is positive, per-trial evidence that non-policy machinery
+decided the episode. Failures a policy can bring on itself stay
+`policy`, so dropping episodes cannot become an escape from a zero.
+Evidence read per trial: Harbor `result.json`/`exception.txt`/`trial.log`,
+the ATIF trajectory (and mini-swe-agent's raw trajectory + log), verifier
+stdout, sibling attempts of the same task, and — when present —
+`broker_audit.jsonl` mapped to trials via the broker session label.
+Thresholds are run-relative (e.g. the run's own fast-decile per-token
+latency) so they do not depend on checkpoint or model size.
+Decisions, by failure family:
+- **Setup / serving / platform first.** Anything that fails before agent
+  execution (env start, agent setup/install, broker create denied/quota,
+  backend errors), trial cancellation, and model-serving API errors
+  (auth, rate limit, connection, 5xx, model-not-found) are `harness`;
+  the policy never acted. `UnicodeDecodeError` from decoding sandbox or
+  terminal output is `harness` (binary output is legitimate in a
+  terminal; the broker path survives it), unless the policy corrupted
+  the reward file being parsed.
+- **"Technical difficulties."** An episode ending in a run of fabricated
+  turns (≥3, burning ≥10% of the agent wall clock) is `harness`: those
+  turns are hardcoded by Terminus-2 after context summarization failed,
+  and the policy never gets a real turn again. Clean context/sequence-
+  length aborts without that loop (summarize-off, MaxSeqLen, response-
+  length abort) are `policy` — the policy's own generations filled the
+  window — except when the *first* prompt alone already exceeds the
+  limit, or the served limit is far below the configured
+  `max_input_tokens`, which are `harness`.
+- **AgentTimeout is `policy` by default** (a policy can always stall),
+  and `harness` only when identifiable time was stolen: extreme
+  per-call latency vs the run's fast baseline, broker exec/timeout
+  stalls on harness operations, one never-returning serving/sandbox
+  call, or uniformly >2× slow serving under which the episode would
+  fit its budget at the run's fast rate. A uniform run-wide slowdown
+  with no in-run contrast is not separable from the policy's own token
+  choices, so it is not dropped.
+- **Verifier timeouts are split by siblings.** If sibling attempts'
+  verifiers already take ≥half the verifier budget (or most siblings
+  time out), the task's verifier is too slow for its budget/resources:
+  `harness`. If siblings verify in seconds, this trial's artifact made
+  the tests hang: `policy`. Missing/unparsable reward files are
+  `harness` unless the policy tampered with `/tests` or verifier paths
+  (checked in the recorded commands, including the broker's send-keys
+  log, which retains the failing batch Harbor never records).
+- **Tmux/session death is `policy` by default.** Only the policy runs
+  commands in the pane, and in the broker run every such case is a
+  policy-issued `tmux kill-*`, `pkill bash`, `exit`/`C-d`, or sourcing a
+  script that replaces/exits the shell. It flips to `harness` only with
+  broker evidence the sandbox was ended externally
+  (`timeout`/`budget`/`shutdown`) or idle-killed between harness execs.
+  Sandbox OOM (exit 137) follows the same before/after-first-command
+  split.
+- **Parse loops.** Malformed replies are `policy`. Replies that are
+  well-structured in the wrong channel/format (JSON in
+  `reasoning_content` with empty content, XML vs a JSON parser) with
+  zero commands ever executed are `harness` when the pattern is strong
+  per-trial or systemic in the run — that is the serving/parser
+  misconfiguration signature, not a policy behaviour. A run where
+  almost no trial ever executes a command is treated the same way.
+- **Broker- and mini-swe-specific paths.** A broker exec-timeout that
+  kills the single long mini-swe-agent exec or the verifier's test
+  script before Harbor's own budget is `harness`; mini-swe step/cost
+  limits and context exhaustion are `policy`; mini install deaths and
+  model-connection deaths (raw exit status / log tail) are `harness`.
+Unknown in-episode crashes after the policy has acted default to
+`policy`: with no positive platform signature, dropping them would pay
+the policy for crash-inducing behaviour. Trials with no `result.json`
+are still covered; with no recorded policy action they are `harness`.
+On the two reference runs this labels 2/640 (pool: one Modal
+`ServiceError` at setup, one TD-loop timeout) and 127/445 (TB2.1 2B:
+122 TD-loop timeouts, 3 sibling-proven verifier timeouts, 2
+single-call serving stalls of ~600 s) as `harness`; everything else,
+including all 12 tmux deaths, the pool verifier hang, and all plain
+verdicts and plain timeouts, stays `policy`.
